title: The retrain rule promotes unless the challenger is clearly worse (dclab-core 0.119.0)
request: The owner, 2026-10-26: 'yes, loosen the retrain rule' (ABL-004: the rule kept champions whose challengers were better later).
spec: CONFIRM.md in agent_runs/live_tests/2026-10-25-retrain-truth, written before the dev tables were read: three conditions.
plan: Read looser rules on ABL-004's 36 train decisions (exploration, so a candidate only).
Fix the confirmation on the dev split's time-ordered tables without twins before reading them.
Only if it passes: RetrainPolicy v2 with promote (unless_clearly_worse by default, only_clearly_better as v1), the schema's v2 baseline, the version.

decisions.decision: Candidate B, promote unless the window's 90% upper bound is below 0.
decisions.why: On the train decisions it missed no gain and promoted 2 worse of 34; the challenger holds the champion's rows and newer ones.

decisions.decision: The dev row floor 1,500 rather than 3,000.
decisions.why: Counted before any dev result: 1 dev table at 3,000 rows, 8 at 1,500; a window then holds 75 rows, above compare's 30.

decisions.decision: v1's rule stays as an option (only_clearly_better).
decisions.why: A host that wants fewer redeploys keeps it; the record says which rule decided.

decisions.decision: Judged only after the five tables OpenML refused (503) were read on a second run.
decisions.why: Three tables alone passed all three conditions on 9 decisions: too few to change a default.

change: dclab_core/retrain.py (RetrainPolicy v2, compare reads promote), schemas/retrain_policy.json and baseline v2, CHANGELOG 0.119.0, __init__ and pyproject; dclab_rnd/agentic/routers/projects.py accepts promote; tests/test_core_retrain.py (the default and the strict rule), tests/test_retrain_studio.py (the kept path under the strict rule); evidence ABL-005.

findings.defect: The retrain rule kept champions whose challengers were better later.
findings.scenario: ABL-004: of 9 champions kept on 13 real time-ordered tables, 5 had a better challenger on the rows after the window.
findings.cause: Promotion needed the window's lower bound above 0: a small window rarely shows a real gain clearly.
findings.fix: Promote unless the window shows the challenger clearly worse (upper bound below the margin).
findings.impact: a model trained on newer rows was kept out for weeks while the old one drifted

measurements.name: ABL-005 dev confirmation
measurements.gate: CONFIRM.md: (1) at most 10% of promotions worse later; (2) at most 50% of kept champions with a better challenger; (3) mean future gain at least v1's, per task with 5 or more decisions
measurements.result: 8 tables, 24 decisions: 23 promoted, 0 worse; 1 kept, 0 missed; mean future gain 0.0223 against v1's 0.0016 (always promoting 0.0209); v1 kept 20 with 6 gains missed
measurements.against_gate: 0 of 23 promotions worse, within 10%; 0 of 1 kept missed, within 50%; 0.0223 >= 0.0016
limits: binary outcomes only on the dev split

outcome: A retrained model replaces the old one unless it is clearly worse on the newest labelled rows; the strict rule remains as an option.
lessons: Confirm a change on tables it was not chosen on; when the downloads fail, finish the run before judging.
risks: More redeploys of equally good models: never a worse one on the window, said in the record's reason.
